newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Clutch of foreign firms in Saigon power revamp.
newsitem.headline: Clutch of foreign firms in Saigon power revamp.

text.p: Thirteen Vietnamese and foreign companies have been selected to provide materials and equipment for a World Bank-financed revamp of the power grid in Ho Chi Minh City, official media reports said on Wednesday.
The Bank's $58 million loan will go towards a three-year project, starting this year, to improve and expand the creaking power network of the country's largest city.
The reports said that three local firms -- Electricity Construction Company No. 2, Hanoi Electricity Meter Company and Minh Long II -- were awarded contracts from more than 100 bidders.
They named the foreign companies as Cimmco, Kabelmetal Indonesia, Switzerland's Sefag, Cooper Industries, Franco Pacific, France's Sicamex, Thailand's ABB Capacitor, Singapore's Comin Asia and Tomen.
